properties.details_shown: Fog, tar, and gulls; the far piers are rotting. Pier four has an upturned skiff where Sela mends a net.

sources.quote: Morning in Gullwick. The fog is still sitting on the docks, gulls everywhere, and you're standing at the end of pier four looking for a boat.
There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net. Grey braid, salt-stained coat. She doesn't look up.

changes.why: Adds the details shown at pier four.

properties.role: Tide-reader who offers to row the party to the old chapel by day.
properties.played_as: Whispers as though the water might hear; avoids eye contact and watches the tide line. Grey braid and salt-stained coat.
properties.knows: Says hers is the only boat that goes near the bell water and that Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang, forty years ago; her grandmother said the water came up warm.

sources.quote: Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.
She talks in a whisper, like the water might hear her, and she never once looks you in the eye. She keeps her gaze on the tide line.
There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net. Grey braid, salt-stained coat. She doesn't look up.
Sela, Sella, the dockhands say it both ways.
Sella's boat is the only one that goes near the bell water. The others are scared.
Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Records the voiced NPC and confirmed spelling variants without treating her claims as verified.

sources.quote: She shrugs and goes back to her net. She says she'll be at pier four tomorrow at first light if you want the ride.

changes.why: Records where the party last saw Sela.

properties.details_shown: Up the cliff path, closed for forty years. Entrance is a black mouth in chalk with a half-rotted timber frame and a rusted cart on its side. Warm air smells of old candle wax. Thirty paces in, warm black water floods the tunnel; wet hymn-book pages float and cling to the walls. One retrieved page has a hymn about the sea giving back what it takes and 'M. Brand' pencilled in the margin.
properties.state: Closed; tunnel flooded with warm black water thirty paces inside.

sources.quote: The Saltmere Mine entrance is a black mouth in the chalk, timber frame half rotted. A rusted cart lies on its side. The air coming out of it is warm and smells like a church, like old candle wax.
About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.
A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".

changes.why: Adds the party's direct observations of the mine and the inscription.

properties.what_is_open: The tunnel contains warm black water and hymn-book pages. Sela's claimed link between the flooding and the bell remains unexplained.

sources.quote: About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.

changes.why: The mine visit supplies direct evidence but does not confirm the historical cause.

properties.what_changed: Mira heard the bell the night she left. Teo now identifies the handwriting of 'M. Brand' on a hymn-book page found in Saltmere as Mira's and believes she was there; the GM has not confirmed that identification.

sources.quote: That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

changes.why: Records Teo's interpretation as progress on his goal, not as proof of Mira's whereabouts.

sources.quote: That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

changes.why: Records the named sister without inferring her location, status, or authorship.

change.name: Is Maren involved with the cult or choir?

properties.what_is_open: Vessa suspects Maren is in the cult and behind the events; Oren suspects she runs the choir. Neither theory is confirmed.

sources.quote: Okay, I bet the harbor-master is behind all this. Maren wanted us gone from day one. She's in the cult, I'm calling it.
Yeah, Maren is totally running the choir.
You can think that. Roll investigation if you want to search the rest.

changes.why: Keeps the players' suspicions in a thread rather than changing Maren.

properties.details_shown: Previously described as having sunk into the bay with its bell. At low water, the bell tower and two broken arches protrude, with seaweed hanging from the stones. At midnight the underwater bell rings twelve times; louder humming can be felt in the teeth. Pale shapes stand in rows on the submerged chapel floor and disappear when the bell stops.

sources.quote: The drowned chapel's roof sticks out of the bay at low water, just the bell tower and two broken arches. Seaweed hangs from the stones.
And then, right at midnight, the bell rings again under the water. Twelve times. And the humming is back, but louder. Much louder than two nights ago. You can feel it in your teeth.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

changes.why: Adds the chapel's visible remains and the witnessed midnight event.

change.name: Fishermen's warning about the Kelp Mother

properties.statement: Fishermen say the Kelp Mother takes children standing close to the water and drags them down by the ankles; its existence is unconfirmed.

sources.quote: Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.
That's what the fishermen say. They pull their boat up and leave.

changes.why: Records local lore without creating a confirmed creature.

sources.quote: You get back to Gullwick by dusk, and you decide to go down to the shore below the old chapel ruins anyway, Sela's warning or not.
Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.

changes.why: Locates the warning at the chapel shore.

sources.quote: (to himself) That's the choir clock at three of six.

changes.why: Advances the existing hidden story clock to the GM's explicit value.

properties.what_is_open: Who or what rings the submerged bell? It rang twelve times at midnight with louder humming; pale shapes stood in rows on the chapel floor and vanished when it stopped.

properties.details_shown: Tavern by the docks, with a fire burning and the smell of tar and fish stew.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.

properties.played_as: Huge, red-bearded; laughs at his own jokes and keeps wiping the same mug. Teases the party as brave or stupid and gives them stew on the house.
properties.knows: Says he has known Maren for thirty years, calls her sharp-tongued with a good heart, and says she lost a brother to the bay.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.
You lot went to the shore at midnight? Brave or stupid. On the house, either way.
Bram is huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, and he wipes the same mug the whole time he talks to you.
Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

properties.next_step: The party plans for Sela to row them out tomorrow at first light, then to dive to the chapel at low tide during the day. Teo believes the mine's hymn pages came from the chapel; their origin is unconfirmed.

sources.quote: Okay, plan. Mira wrote in that hymn book. The chapel is where the hymns came from. We go down to the chapel.
At low tide, during the day. Not at night, Sela was right about that.
